verdict.reasoning: Patient reports “a cough and a sore throat for about a week” and requests “reassurance… anything you can prescribe me… or maybe even a sick note.”
Patient states sore throat was “about last week. Friday or Thursday. Cough was Saturday or Sunday,” and cough described as “very dry,” i.e., non-productive.
Patient confirms shortness of breath and wheeze/chest pain: “Yeah… Yes.” Onset: “shortly after the cough… So three, four days ago?”

Patient says breathlessness occurs with exertion but is not limiting: “when I'm doing walking and I do exercise now and then… it hasn't stopped me from doing any of those things,” in response to a question about severity including climbing stairs.
Patient reports fever early in illness: “a little bit feverish at first, so the first three or so days of this, but then the fever's gone away.”
Patient adds: “also had a bit of a headache, like headaches that come and go rather.”
Patient: “no weight loss. But I have been… losing my appetite recently… but you haven't lost any weight that you think of? Patient: No, not that.”
Patient describes fluctuation: “I felt better and then worse again, and then better and then worse again. So it's been a kind of constant, but constant in being variable.”
Doctor asks, “you're not coughing up blood or anything like that?” Patient replies, “No, no.”
Patient states cough is “very dry” and “no, you're not coughing up any phlegm,” indicating absence of purulent sputum.
Doctor: “you say you have a cold, so do you have sinus congestion or—” Patient: “No, it seems to be almost entirely with just my throat.”
Patient: “in terms of recent travel, just to Europe, nowhere too exotic,” and doctor summarizes “no significant recent travel anywhere.”
Transcript: “No past medical history? No.” There is no discussion of surgical history, so stating “no… surgical history” adds undocumented information.
Doctor: “Are you taking any medications currently at the moment?” Patient: “No, I'm not.”
Patient: “Not to any medication, but I'm allergic to peanuts.”
Patient: “my mother had lung cancer.” Doctor repeats, “Your mother had lung cancer.”

Doctor asks about clots: “No one in your family's had those clots in the legs or lungs?” Patient provides only lung cancer for mother and adds “No, no, that's the only one,” implying no family DVT/PE history.
Patient: “Do you smoke? No… I mean, once or twice in Amsterdam, but not really.” This supports non-smoker with brief experimentation.
Doctor: “Have you ever smoked or been exposed to asbestos?” Patient: “You know, don't know if asbestos… ever smoked… once or twice….” This indicates no known asbestos exposure.
Patient: “I was born in the US and moved over about 12 years ago.” The context is residence in the UK.
Patient mentions work absence: “I've had to stay away from work for about three or four of those days,” indicating current employment.
Clinician describes course and offers reassurance but does not explicitly state a diagnostic impression such as “viral URTI” or “pharyngitis,” nor labels wheeze as mild.
Patient: “I've had to stay away from work for about three or four of those days because of a badness.” This is recognized during the assessment.

Patient expresses concern after googling: mentions “cancer always comes up,” and doctor later refers to “Your concerns about lung cancer, was that the other thing…” and says he wouldn’t be concerned about tuberculosis, reflecting anxiety about these diagnoses.
Doctor: “paracetamol, lots of fluids, and rest up,” consistent with treatment of a presumed viral upper respiratory infection based on prior discussion.
Doctor: “expect this to sort of be getting better in the next four or five days.”

Safety net: doctor advises to seek care if “you feel significantly worse, if you get more short of breath or sudden change in your breathlessness,” and “If it's not [better in 4–5 days], please get in touch.” There is no mention of emergency department specifically, nor chest pain or sustained fever as triggers, and timeframe stated is 4–5 days, not “more than one week.”
Doctor: “I'll provide you with a sick note just to give you a few more days off work.”

Doctor: “I wouldn't be concerned about tuberculosis. Your concerns about lung cancer… if you're not getting better, please see somebody again,” which is reassurance about low likelihood of serious disease with advice for re-review if symptoms persist.
